statements.t: Meeting the Company's forecasts and budgets;

During the second quarter of 2026, activities at the Johnson Tract Project focused on planning, resourcing, permitting coordination, and logistical preparations in support of the Company’s planned 2026 field program.
Completion of the pad this year advances site preparation ahead of schedule and allows the Company to begin selecting engineering consultants for the new camp, which is targeted for 2027.
The Company anticipates from time to time acquiring additional properties in Alaska for exploration, subject to the availability of funds.

The Company is guiding towards the lower end of its 2026 production guidance of 40,000 gold equivalent ounces attributable to its 30% interest in the Peak Gold JV with 2026 cash costs and AISC of $2,700 and $2,900 per ounce of gold sold, respectively.

The Company’s primary cash requirements have been for general and administrative expenses, capital calls from the Peak Gold JV for the Manh Choh Project, repayment of principal and interest related to debt and exploration expenditures on the Johnson Tract Project, Lucky Shot Property and Kitsault Valley Project.
The Company’s cash needs going forward will primarily relate to exploration of the Contango Properties, repayment of debt and related interest and general and administrative expenses of the Company.

Although there can be no guarantee that the Peak Gold JV will continue to make distributions to the Company, the Company believes that distributions are probable and that it will maintain sufficient liquidity to meet its working capital requirements, including repayment obligations of approximately $45.3 million on the Facility (see at Note 13 - Debt), for the next twelve months from the date of this report.

The Company expects to fund these longer-term obligations through a combination of anticipated cash distributions from the Peak Gold JV, proceeds from metal sales, potential future equity issuances (including amounts available under its ATM Program), and available cash on hand.

The content of the Company’s website is not incorporated by reference into this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q or in any other report or document it files with the SEC, and any references to the Company’s website is intended to be inactive textual references only.

statements.t: Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer said, “The focus for the third quarter was to continue to advance and de-risk our portfolio of advanced-stage exploration projects.

Operational enhancements continue to be made ahead of our fourth 2026 campaign, scheduled to commence in mid-November with anticipated production of 13,000 to 15,000 gold equivalent ounces net to Contango, keeping us on track to meet the lower end of 2026 production guidance of 40,000 gold equivalent ounces.
The Company expects to provide 2027 production and cost guidance later in December.”
We will continue to release assay results in batches as they are received.
We expect to have all assays received and QAQC’s by January 2027 and then complete an updated mineral resource estimate (“MRE”) in the first half of 2027.
We expect to complete this work by February 2027.

Once all assays are received and QAQC’d, the Company plans to provide an updated MRE, scheduled for first half of 2027, which will form the basis of a feasibility study targeted for release in late 2027.”

On a consolidated basis in Q3, the Company reported a total loss from operations of $24.2 M, net loss of $23.0 M and an adjusted net loss 1 of $20.9 M, primarily related to expensed exploration across all projects.
Ore transportation from the Manh Choh mine to the Fort Knox milling facility continues to outperform and is expected to exceed our planned budget for 2026.

The Company is guiding towards the lower end of its 2026 production guidance of 40,000 gold equivalent ounces attributable to its 30% interest in the Peak Gold JV with 2026 cash costs and AISC of $2,700 and $2,900 per ounce of gold sold 2 , respectively.

Updated Mineral Resource Estimate: On September 11, 2026, the Company reported an updated MRE for the Kitsault Valley Project comprising 7.66 million tonnes of indicated resources containing 58.70 million ounces of silver and 394.70 thousand ounces of gold (89.55 million ounces AgEq), and approximately 6.31 million tonnes of inferred resources containing 22.80 million ounces of silver and 620.82 thousand ounces…
In H1-2027 the Company is planning to update the MRE with the drilling completed in 2026, which will form the basis of the IA targeted for release in late 2027.
Management uses Adjusted Net Income/(Loss) to evaluate the Company’s operating performance, and to plan and forecast operations.

The shares will be offered pursuant to the Company’s effective automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-297038) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on June 25, 2026 and the related prospectus supplement dated November 13, 2026.
The Company intends to use the net proceeds from any sales under the ATM Program, if any, for general corporate purposes.
